_comment: The write guard matches Bash as well as the edit tools, and that is not belt and braces. The first
version matched Write|Edit only, and the first person to test it walked straight through: their
session was configured to make file changes with sed and heredocs, so a `sed -i` on a generated
artefact was never offered to the hook. A guard that covers only the paths nobody takes produces
confidence instead of protection, which is the exact failure this plugin exists to argue against.
It costs about 220ms per matching call, measured, all of it PowerShell process startup - so roughly
a fifth of a second on every edit and every shell command. That is the price of the guard holding,
and it is the honest trade rather than a free one. Remove the Bash alternative from the matcher if
your sessions never write through the shell and you want those milliseconds back.
A third hook, Note-BuildRanDump.ps1, still ships off: it would be a second process spawn on every
Bash call to say something that only applies after a build. docs/10-hooks.md has the block to paste.
Hooks add no always-on tokens: claude plugin details reports them as harness-only.
